title: Rama, who keeps the bounds
hookLine: Lakshmana's greatest victory, and the same day, Indrajit comes back with Brahma's weapon
carry: maryada: lines rama won't cross, even to win
last: DHARMA FIRST, EVEN BEFORE A BROTHER.

cards: With Kumbhakarna gone, Ravana sends out his other sons. One of them, Atikaya, is a giant in armor that Brahma himself gave him, and no arrow will go through it. Lakshmana fights him a long time, getting nowhere.
Then, Valmiki says, the wind god Vayu comes close and whispers in Lakshmana's ear: that armor came from Brahma. Only Brahma's own weapon will break it. Lakshmana takes the hint, and Atikaya falls.
It's Lakshmana's great victory. It doesn't last the day.

teach.b: Indrajit comes back. Several of his brothers, his uncle Kumbhakarna and a string of champions are dead, and he's furious. This time he prepares.
Before he rides out, he makes offerings into a sacred fire, and he comes out with a chariot that can't be seen.
Then, from out of sight again, he invokes the weapon of Brahma, the creator. It isn't one arrow. It's a storm.
Valmiki pictures the whole field covered: Sugriva, Angada, Jambavan, Nila, leader after leader falling.
And Rama does something surprising. He knows what this weapon is, and he chooses not to fight it. This is Brahma's weapon, he tells Lakshmana; it deserves respect.
Let's endure it. So the two brothers stand in the rain of arrows and fall, side by side once again. Indrajit rides home in triumph.
Hanuman did the same thing in Lanka, when Indrajit bound him with this very weapon: he honored Brahma's power and let himself be bound.
This is why Hindus call Rama Maryada Purushottama, the best of men, who keeps the maryada, the bounds.

teach.h: LINES HE WON'T CROSS, EVEN TO WIN.
teach.b: Even at war, even when it costs him, there are lines he won't cross to win: not against what is sacred, not against his word. The battlefield is left at night, quiet, strewn with the fallen.
Somewhere among them, a few are still awake.

how: Rama is widely called Maryada Purushottama, the best of men who keeps the bounds, and tellers often point to his choice to endure Brahma's weapon, set beside the serpent-arrows earlier in the war.

o: the day Lakshmana is cursed by an angry forest sage
the hour Lakshmana loses his bow to Atikaya's armor
the night Lakshmana and Rama fall to Brahma's weapon

games.q: the day's turns — tap the pairs.

s: Lakshmana defeats Atikaya with an ordinary arrow
the wind god tells him only Brahma's weapon can pierce Brahma's armor.
Rama chooses not to fight Brahma's weapon
he says the creator's weapon deserves respect, and they endure it.
Maryada Purushottama means Rama wins by any means
it means the best of men, who keeps the bounds, even when it costs him.

games.q: you're Rama. Indrajit, unseen, has released the weapon of Brahma, the creator. what do you do?
o: counter it with your own weapons.
games.why: Rama tells Lakshmana that Brahma's weapon deserves respect, and they let it strike them: Maryada Purushottama keeps the bounds, even at war.

practice: Sit still and feel the edges of the body, where you end and the room begins. A boundary can hold you, not only hem you in. If you pray, say Rama's name slowly with the breath, Ram on the in-breath, Ram on the out-breath.
If you don't, bring to mind one line you keep even when crossing it would be easier, and rest there.

wordCard.voice: Lakshmana wounded. On the day of his great victory over Atikaya, he and Rama fall to Indrajit's Brahma weapon, which Rama, keeping the bounds, chooses to endure.

orig.note: Sanskrit brahmāstra: the weapon of Brahma, from brahma and astra, a weapon invoked with a mantra.

carryVoice: Your line: maryada, lines Rama won't cross, even to win. Two survivors are about to walk the field with torches. Rest well.
